races.title: State Assembly, District 28
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Gail Pellerin
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 28 since December 2022. Previously Santa Cruz County Clerk and chief elections official (clerk from 2004 until retiring in December 2020; in the elections office since 1993), and spent over seven years in Assembly staff roles. Chairs the Assembly Elections Committee.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, SEIU Local 521, California Environmental Voters and Equality California.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance or action by her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth limits, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, abortion or school choice. Her campaign site lists general priorities (housing, jobs, health care, climate, education, public safety) without specific positions. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, and her 2022 survey answers were general. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages we had. Her sponsored-bill list on Ballotpedia was empty in the page we read, so we could not review her bills.

local.label: Roots 90: She was born in Torrance, graduated from Santa Ynez Valley High School in 1980 and Cal Poly San Luis Obispo in 1984, and has lived in Santa Cruz County since 1993.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Current Assembly member since 2022. Santa Cruz County Clerk and chief elections official for about 27 years, elected clerk unopposed. Earlier held positions in the state Assembly for over seven years, including assistant director of the Speaker's Office of Majority Services.
qual.why: She has prior and current legislative service, years of Assembly staff work, and long executive experience running a county office (she has taught credential courses on budgets), which fits the high band for writing law and the budget. Committee chairmanships were not counted.

cands.name: Carol Pefley
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 28 in 2026. Real estate broker who founded her own Silicon Valley brokerage in 2009, with about 45 agents under her license. Worked for many years in television news and radio broadcasting. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Republican Party of California and Reform California. It also lists voter-guide recommendations from April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Carol Pefley grew up in the U.S. or when she came to California. We found no record of elected office or legislative work, and no record of anything she has done in office. Her campaign site lists blog posts on immigration, housing and other topics, but only the titles were available, so we left out her views on those. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, police pay, guns, abortion or school choice. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the sources we had.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Founded a real estate brokerage in Silicon Valley in 2009 and grew it to about 45 agents; earlier worked in television news and radio broadcasting after earning a broadcast journalism degree. No prior elected office or legislative or policy staff work is shown.
qual.why: She is a business owner and manager, which fits the middle band. No legislative, policy or budget career or elected office is shown, so she scores no higher.
qual.label: She is a business owner and manager, which fits the middle band. No legislative, policy or budget career or elected office is shown, so she scores no higher.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Said in her ballot statement that she believes in "responsible, coordinated growth that works with communities, not sweeping mandates that override local planning," and that state decisions accelerate overdevelopment and strain local infrastructure.

clean-money.evidence: Pledged in her ballot statement: "I will not be influenced by corporate interests or donors who don't understand our communities."

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In her ballot statement she criticizes state housing mandates that she says bypass local input and "accelerate overdevelopment, strain our infrastructure," and says she supports responsible, coordinated growth decided locally.
